unit_description: This unit focuses on geometry. Students describe shapes using sides and vertices, identify parallel sides and quadrilaterals, and classify squares, rectangles, rhombuses, parallelograms, and trapezoids.
unit_goals: Describe shapes using sides and vertices.
Classify and draw parallelograms and trapezoids.
Use attributes to name and sort quadrilaterals.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students describe and classify two-dimensional shapes, focusing on quadrilaterals and their attributes.

lessons.lesson_title: Describe Shapes Using Sides and Vertices
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by counting sides and vertices of familiar shapes.
lessons.concept: Polygons are named by their number of sides and vertices. A side is a straight edge, and a vertex is a corner where two sides meet.
lessons.practice: Identify the number of sides and vertices for polygons.
lessons.objective: Describe shapes using sides and vertices.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by counting sides and vertices.

questions.prompt: How many sides does a triangle have?
How many vertices does a rectangle have?
What is the name for a straight edge of a shape?
questions.hint: A straight edge is called a side.

learn.title: Describe Shapes Using Sides and Vertices
teaching_points: Count the sides to name the shape.
Sides and vertices are important attributes.

example.equation: A pentagon has 5 sides and 5 vertices.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: How many sides and vertices does a hexagon have?
try_it.hint: A hexagon has 6 sides and 6 vertices.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Count the sides and vertices of each shape.

bigIdea.title: Describe Shapes Using Sides and Vertices
bigIdea.subtitle: Count the edges and corners
bigIdea.intro: Every polygon has straight sides and vertices. We can describe shapes by counting how many of each they have.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why are the number of sides and vertices always the same for a polygon?

ruleCards.description: A side is a straight line segment in a polygon.
A vertex is where two sides meet.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by tracing pairs of sides that never cross.
lessons.concept: Parallel sides are sides that stay the same distance apart and never cross. A quadrilateral is a polygon with exactly four sides.
lessons.practice: Identify parallel sides and name quadrilaterals.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has how many pairs of parallel sides?
How many sides does a quadrilateral have?
A trapezoid has at least how many parallel sides?
questions.hint: At least one pair of parallel sides.

learn.title: Identify Parallel Sides and Quadrilaterals
teaching_points: Parallel sides never cross and stay the same distance apart.
A quadrilateral has 4 sides and 4 vertices.
Quadrilaterals can have 0, 1, or 2 pairs of parallel sides.

example.prompt: What is the name of a shape with 4 sides and two pairs of parallel sides?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: How many pairs of parallel sides does a parallelogram have?
try_it.hint: A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Identify the number of parallel side pairs in each quadrilateral.

bigIdea.title: Identify Parallel Sides and Quadrilaterals
bigIdea.subtitle: Look for sides that never cross
bigIdea.intro: Parallel sides are straight edges that stay the same distance apart. A quadrilateral is any four-sided polygon. These two attributes help us name and classify shapes.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How can you tell if two sides are parallel?

ruleCards.description: Parallel sides never meet, no matter how far they are extended.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by sorting shapes into square, rectangle, and rhombus groups.
lessons.concept: Squares, rectangles, and rhombuses are all parallelograms. A square has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. A rectangle has 4 right angles. A rhombus has 4 equal sides.
lessons.practice: Classify squares, rectangles, and rhombuses by their attributes.

questions.prompt: A shape has 4 right angles and opposite sides equal. Is it a square or a rectangle?
questions.hint: It could be a rectangle; a square also has equal sides.

questions.prompt: A shape has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. What is it?
questions.hint: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles.

questions.prompt: A shape has 4 equal sides but no right angles. What is it?

learn.title: Classify Squares, Rectangles, and Rhombuses
teaching_points: A square is a rectangle with 4 equal sides.
A square is also a rhombus with 4 right angles.
Use side length and angle size to classify.

example.prompt: Classify a shape with 4 right angles and 4 equal sides.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A parallelogram has 4 equal sides but no right angles. What is it?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Classify each shape as a square, rectangle, or rhombus.

flashcards.title: Squares, Rectangles, Rhombuses
flashcards.instructions: Review attributes of squares, rectangles, and rhombuses.

bigIdea.title: Classify Squares, Rectangles, and Rhombuses
bigIdea.subtitle: Use side and angle attributes
bigIdea.intro: A square is a special shape: it is both a rectangle and a rhombus. A rectangle has right angles. A rhombus has equal sides. A square has both.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How are a square, rectangle, and rhombus related?

ruleCards.description: A rectangle has four right angles.
A rhombus has four equal sides.

lessons.lesson_title: Classify and Draw Parallelograms and Trapezoids
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by drawing quadrilaterals with parallel sides.
lessons.concept: A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides. A trapezoid has at least one pair of parallel sides. We can draw these shapes using the parallel-side rule.
lessons.practice: Classify and draw parallelograms and trapezoids.
lessons.objective: Classify and draw parallelograms and trapezoids.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up with parallelograms and trapezoids.

questions.prompt: A parallelogram has how many pairs of parallel sides?
questions.hint: Two pairs of opposite sides parallel.

questions.prompt: A trapezoid has at least how many pairs of parallel sides?
questions.hint: At least one pair of parallel sides.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is a special kind of what?
questions.hint: A rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides.

learn.title: Classify and Draw Parallelograms and Trapezoids
teaching_points: Parallelogram: two pairs of parallel sides.
Trapezoid: at least one pair of parallel sides.
Draw parallel lines to make these shapes.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Draw a quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides. What is it called?
try_it.hint: A trapezoid has at least one pair of parallel sides.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Classify each quadrilateral and draw a parallelogram and a trapezoid.

bigIdea.title: Classify and Draw Parallelograms and Trapezoids
bigIdea.subtitle: Use parallel sides
bigIdea.intro: Parallelograms and trapezoids are named by their parallel sides. A parallelogram has two pairs. A trapezoid has at least one pair. These parallel sides help you draw and classify them.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What is the difference between a parallelogram and a trapezoid?

ruleCards.description: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.

ruleCards.equation: at least 1 pair of parallel sides
ruleCards.description: A trapezoid has at least one pair of parallel sides.

lessons.fact_drill: Rapid review of sides and vertices, parallel sides, squares/rectangles/rhombuses, and parallelograms/trapezoids.
lessons.concept: Review the four big ideas from this unit: sides and vertices, parallel sides and quadrilaterals, squares/rectangles/rhombuses, and parallelograms/trapezoids.
lessons.practice: Complete a balanced evaluation covering the skills from this unit.
lessons.objective: Show what you know about quadrilaterals.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Get ready to show what you know.

questions.prompt: How many sides does a quadrilateral have?
A parallelogram has how many pairs of parallel sides?
A square has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. Is it a rhombus?
questions.hint: A square is a special rhombus.

learn.title: Ready to Show What You Know
teaching_points: Use any strategy that helps you.

example.prompt: You have learned four big ideas this unit.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A shape has 4 sides and 4 right angles but not all sides equal. What is it?

practice_block.title: Unit Evaluation
practice_block.instructions: Answer all questions carefully to show your understanding.

flashcards.title: Unit 33 Review
flashcards.instructions: Review key terms from Unit 33 before the evaluation.

bigIdea.title: Unit Evaluation: Quadrilaterals
bigIdea.subtitle: Show what you know
bigIdea.intro: This evaluation checks your understanding of the four big ideas from this unit: sides and vertices, parallel sides and quadrilaterals, squares/rectangles/rhombuses, and parallelograms/trapezoids.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you know about quadrilaterals?

ruleCards.description: A quadrilateral has 4 sides and 4 vertices.
A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides.
